newsitem.title: UK: British Sugar sees above average UK sugar output.
newsitem.headline: British Sugar sees above average UK sugar output.

text.p: British Sugar expects final sugar output from the 1996/97 beet crop to be above the average result for the last five years, according to the latest edition of the British Sugar Beet Review.
The review, published by British Sugar plc and the Sugar Beet Research and Education Fund, said the crop was returning the highest average percentage sugar content for many years.
Average contents during October and November were reported at around 19 percent, compared with 16.5 percent for 1995/96.
Despite a more pessimistic outlook at the end of the summer, improved conditions in the autumn had boosted the overall output estimate, it said.
"The beet responded superbly to the ideal growing conditions that were a feature of the autumn months," the review said.
"British Sugar says that the growth it made during September and October was unprecedented and, as a result, the company is confidently expecting an above average final result."
A company spokesman said the average production over the last five year was around 1.25 million tonnes but added that the company had yet to release its own estimate of outturn.

The Sugar Beet Review said output at British Sugar factories had been maintained at well above average levels, which had more than recovered the delayed start at the company's flagship processing plant at Wissington.
Growers were delivering a high quality, disease-free crop but careful long-term storage would be crucial due to the colder weather comditions, it said.
